cannibalization_risks.primary_competing_keyword: slatmill vs walk / dog treadmill vs walk
cannibalization_risks.evidence: Both posts answer the same question — walk vs. slatmill/treadmill — with overlapping H2 structure, the same SlatmillExplainer component, and near-identical conclusions. P7 is substantially longer (~1,150 words), has a differentiated breed-specific angle, and already has better keyword targeting in the title/slug. P5 is 500 words, less structured, and is fully subsumed by P7 in coverage.
cannibalization_risks.recommendation: Redirect P5 (/blog/slatmill-vs-long-walk/) to P7 (/blog/dog-treadmill-vs-walk-comparison/). Preserve any unique P5 content — specifically the Florida/weather section — by merging it into P7 before redirecting. Update all internal links pointing to P5.

cannibalization_risks.primary_competing_keyword: high energy dog breeds exercise / breeds that need more than a walk
cannibalization_risks.evidence: Both posts list the same 6-7 breeds (Malinois, Ridgeback, Husky, Border Collie, Shepherd, Vizsla/Weimaraner), both explain why walks do not work, both end with a slatmill CTA. P6 has better depth (~700w, 7 named breeds, 'why walks fail' math section, 'what actually works' section). P8 (~650w) is structurally thinner with shorter breed blurbs. P8's slug contains the keyword 'need-more-than-a-walk' which overlaps directly with P6's title.
cannibalization_risks.recommendation: Keep P6 (/blog/high-energy-dog-breeds-exercise-guide/) as canonical. Migrate P8's unique content (Kai origin story paragraph, shorter punchy format) into P6 as an intro or sidebar element. Redirect P8 to P6.

cannibalization_risks.evidence: P2 and P3 target adjacent but distinct queries. P2 = 'how to tire out' (method-focused), P3 = 'how much exercise' (quantity-focused). Both mention the same insufficiency of walks, both recommend slatmill, both target the same high-drive dog owner. SERP overlap is ~6/10 — same cluster but defensibly different.
cannibalization_risks.recommendation: Keep both but differentiate more aggressively. P3 should focus purely on diagnosis/quantity (signals of under-exercise, breed drive levels, time requirements). P2 should focus purely on method/tactics (what types of exercise work, slatmill mechanics, protocol). Add explicit cross-links between them in both directions. Ensure P2 title and meta do not use quantity framing and P3 does not use method framing.

cannibalization_risks.evidence: P1 is a 350-word brand manifesto that partially covers the same ground as P2 (why structure matters, what owners notice). It has no standalone ranking keyword and is too thin to rank independently.
cannibalization_risks.recommendation: Expand P1 into a true pillar on 'canine conditioning science' OR convert it to a long-form piece targeting 'why structured exercise matters for dogs' with a clear differentiation from P2. Alternatively, redirect to P2 and use its content as P2's introduction section.
